subject: ss-infectious-diseases
title: HACEK Organisms and Miscellaneous Gram-Negative Bacteria

steps.tx: **HACEK** is an acronym for fastidious, slow-growing gram-negative bacteria that need carbon dioxide enrichment and do not grow on MacConkey agar. The group includes Haemophilus, Aggregatibacter, Cardiobacterium, Eikenella corrodens and Kingella kingae. They are commensals of the oral cavity. Their slow growth delays culture positivity and makes susceptibility testing difficult.

steps.tx: A positive **HACEK blood culture** strongly predicts underlying infective endocarditis, with an overall positive predictive value near 60%. The value varies by organism: it is high with Aggregatibacter bacteraemia but very low with Eikenella. HACEK causes roughly 0.8 to 6% of endocarditis, mainly aortic and mitral valves. Echocardiography should follow any positive culture.

steps.tx: HACEK endocarditis tends to affect younger patients and causes many embolic and immunologic features. Vegetations are seen on echocardiography in up to 85% of cases. Treatment is a prolonged course of intravenous **ceftriaxone**, a third-generation cephalosporin, as first-line therapy. Prognosis is excellent and better than non-HACEK endocarditis.

steps.tx: **Kingella kingae** behaves differently from other HACEK organisms. More than half of its infections are bone and joint infections, and colonisation peaks before age 3 years. It can cause a petechial rash resembling **Neisseria meningitidis** sepsis. Molecular methods such as 16S rRNA PCR and MALDI-TOF help identify it, and synovial fluid can be inoculated into blood culture bottles.
